notes: Packet defects. F1 is the table-of-contents graphic (twin-boundary cartoon, CO2 -> C2H4) and F2 is a journal-cover thumbnail; neither is a paper figure, both carry empty captions, and both are offered as whole-figure panel ids. Packet F3-F7 are paper Figures 1-5. In F7 the caption assigns (c) to the (113) surface and (d) to (111), but the panels themselves are annotated La2CuO4 (111) and La2CuO4 (113) respectively, i.e. the caption letters are swapped; o16 follows the on-panel labels. Text-figure mismatches: the F6 linked text places the EXAFS Cu-O and Cu-La peaks at 1.9 and 3.2 A while the plotted uncorrected R+alpha axis reads about 1.5 and 3.0 A (o14 image_note); the F5 linked text calls the 12 h current 'stable ... only subtle fluctuation' while the NB trace grows about 40% in magnitude (o9, image_support partial). Argument. One main branch (heating rate -> twin boundaries -> strain -> longer Cu-O/Cu-La bonds -> stronger CO* binding) joins a parallel DFT branch ((113) gap states -> electron transfer -> 0.38 eV C-C coupling barrier) at the C2H4 performance node n16, which carries the paper's own two-cause statement as joint causes edges; boundary-free bulk La2CuO4 is the control branch (n17) linked to n16 by contrasts. Information lost: the SI carries the NR and bulk PXRD/EDS/ICP, the EXAFS fits (Table S4) on which the bond-lengthening claim rests, the LSV, the NMR liquid-product analysis and the literature comparison (Table S3); n10 therefore has image_support not_shown and basis argued. Four audits, all figure-only readings the text does not state: a1 (no resolvable bond lengthening in F6d), a2 (CO2 adsorption ranks opposite to C2H4 selectivity), a3 (the CO TPD ranking spans 9 C on 100 C wide peaks), a4 (bulk FE totals exceed 100%). No DSC/design_guidance node was written (the heating-rate rule is carried by k3 and n4) to keep the node count near the protocol budget.

pairs.cause: electrospinning followed by calcination at 700 C for 2 h in air at 1 C/min
pairs.effect: La2CuO4 nanobamboo morphology with rich twin boundaries and strain-induced Cu-O and Cu-La bond-length changes
pairs.note: n5->n6->n7/n8 and n8->n9->n10 carry the whole chain, with k3 as the heating-rate precedent. The bond-length element is the weak link: n10 has image_support not_shown and basis argued because the EXAFS fits are in Table S4, and audit a1 records that the F6d transforms superpose in peak position.

pairs.cause: presence of twin boundaries and induced strain in La2CuO4 NBs
pairs.effect: enhanced Faradaic efficiency toward ethylene in CO2RR
pairs.note: both branches into n16 are present and marked joint: strain -> longer Cu-O/Cu-La bonds -> stronger CO* binding -> C-C coupling (n9-n12), and the (113) gap states -> electron transfer -> 0.38 eV barrier (n13-n15). Audits a2 and a3 qualify the TPD leg (CO2 binding ranks opposite to C2H4 selectivity; the CO ranking spans 9 C on 100 C wide peaks). The MatMech sub-claim that DFT gives (113) a lower CO2 adsorption energy has no node; the graph's DFT nodes are gap states and the C-C coupling barrier.

pairs.effect: superior CO2RR performance compared with other Cu-based catalysts
pairs.note: the graph has no DSC/comparison node and no node asserting the literature verdict: the comparison rests on Table S3, which is not in the packet, and survives only as attrs.note on n16. Cause and effect also collapse onto the same fact (the 60% FE), so the pair is not a causal link the graph could carry.
